home.cardExpensesInfoBody1: Everything charged to your credit cards this month — a swipe, an online purchase, a UPI payment made on the card. To see each one, open Expenses and pick the Card filter.
home.cardExpensesInfoBody2: Card spending is never added to bank expenses above. That money has not left your bank yet; it leaves when you pay the bill.
home.billPaidInfoBody1: Money that reached your credit cards this month and settled what you had already spent on them. To see each payment, open Income and pick the Card filter.
home.billPaidInfoBody2: A bill paid straight from your bank also counts in bank expenses, because that money left your account. It is never added to card expenses — those spends were counted on the day you made them.
home.billPaidInfoBody3: Paid through other apps? The amount that reached the card is shown here, while the debit that funded it stays in bank expenses under that app's name, so nothing is counted twice.
home.bankExpensesInfoBody1: Everything that left your bank and cash accounts this month: UPI and card-free payments, cheques, ATM withdrawals, standing instructions, and anything you added by hand. Each one counts on its own date, and tapping the tile lists them all.
home.bankExpensesInfoBody2: Credit card spending is not counted here. It belongs to the card until you settle it, so it sits in the Credit card row below instead — the money is still in your account.
home.bankExpensesInfoBody3: A credit card bill paid from your bank is counted here, on the day it left the account. That is the moment card spending finally reaches your bank, and it is counted only once: as a bank expense, never again as a card expense.
home.bankExpensesInfoBody4: Moving money to another of your own accounts also counts, because it really did leave this one. The account that received it records the matching income, so your balance is unchanged.
home.bankExpensesInfoBody5: Accounts you marked as excluded are left out entirely, and so is anything dated outside this month.
home.sumCardBillsPaid: credit card bills paid from it
home.sumBankExpensesNote: This is why the figure can look large in a month you paid a bill: a bill is money out of the bank, even though you spent it earlier.
home.sumEverythingSpentNote: The bill you paid sits inside the first line, since that money left your bank this month. The card spending it settles was counted on the card in the month you made it, so a bill for older spending is counted in this month as well as in that one.
home.bankIncomeInfoBody1: Everything that arrived in your bank and cash accounts this month: salary, interest, refunds, money received over UPI, and anything you added by hand. Tap the tile to see each one.
home.bankIncomeInfoBody2: Money moved in from another of your own accounts is counted, because this account did receive it. The account it came from carries the matching expense.
home.bankIncomeInfoBody3: A payment that reaches your credit card is not income. It clears what you owe on the card, so it appears as Bill paid in the Credit card row below.
home.sumLeftBank: left them, the bank expenses shown
home.sumBalanceNote: What left your accounts includes the credit card bill you paid this month, which is why a month with a bill can come out lower than it feels.
home.bankBalanceInfoBody1: This month's bank income minus this month's bank expenses. Nothing else is in it, so the two figures beside it always add up to this one.
home.bankBalanceInfoBody2: It is not the money you hold today. Whatever your accounts carried in from earlier months is not part of it — open Accounts to see those running totals.
home.bankBalanceInfoBody3: A figure below zero simply means more left your accounts this month than arrived, which often happens when a credit card bill for earlier spending falls in it.

alarms.enableInfo:
The master switch for reminders. With it on, a reminder arrives as a phone notification at its time, whether Kashio is open or not, and opens the app with Done and Snooze when you tap it.

With it off, nothing arrives at all.

Use the two switches below to decide whether reminders make a sound and whether they vibrate. The notification itself always appears.
alarms.soundHint: Play the alarm tone when a reminder is due
alarms.offKeepsChoices: Reminders are off, so nothing will ring or arrive and anything already booked has been cancelled. The settings below are greyed out but keep your choices, ready for when you turn reminders back on.
alarms.toneSaved: Saved. That is what a reminder will sound like while Kashio is open, on your phone’s alarm volume.
alarms.toneBackToBuiltIn: Reminders are back to Kashio's own tone.
alarms.toneUnplayable: Your phone would not play that tone, so Kashio’s own one is ringing instead. A tone that was moved or deleted does this — pick another of the phone’s alarm sounds, or tap Kashio’s tone to settle for that.
alarms.toneUnavailable: This phone did not offer its alarm tones, so Kashio's own tone stays in use.
alarms.toneNotReceived: Your phone did not tell Kashio which tone you picked, so nothing changed. Try once more, and pick one of the phone's own alarm sounds rather than a tone you added yourself.
alarms.toneClosedAppNote: Applies while Kashio is open. A reminder arriving with the app closed uses your phone's notification sound, which Android alone controls.
alarms.vibrationHint: Vibrate when a reminder is due
alarms.blocked: Notifications are turned off for Kashio in your phone's settings, so reminders cannot reach you while the app is closed.
alarms.unsupported: This build cannot post phone notifications, so reminders only reach you while Kashio is open. Installing the latest version fixes it.
alarms.quiet: Sound and vibration are both off, so reminders will arrive silently.
alarms.testBody: You should hear a short alarm tone and feel it vibrate.
alarms.testQuiet: Sound and vibration are both off, so a real reminder would arrive silently as a notification.
alarms.testMediaHint: Heard nothing? Android plays app sounds through the media volume, not the alarm volume, so turn the media volume up with the side buttons while something is playing and test again.
alarms.testNoSoundBody:
This phone could not play the alarm sound.

Check that media volume is up and the phone is not on silent or Do Not Disturb. If that is not it, the app needs rebuilding — the sound player is missing from this build.

cards.lead: Statements from your card SMS land here. Mark a bill paid when you have settled it.
cards.aboutSms: These figures are read from credit-card SMS. They are a guide — not the exact amount on the bank statement.

cards.aboutCycle: The statement total and current expenses are for this card’s billing cycle — from the statement date to today — not for the calendar month.
cards.aboutHome: Do not compare these with expenses on Home. Home adds up the whole month, including every account, not one card cycle.

cards.refreshOff: An admin has turned credit card bill reminders off.
cards.addLead: Type the bank and last 4. Statement date, due date, and total due are optional if Refresh can read them from SMS.
cards.addSharedDatesCopied: This bank’s cards share one credit limit, so statement date, due date, and amount copy from the other cards. Type the last 4 only.

cards.sharedLimitLead: You have {n} {issuer} cards ending {last4s}. Do they share one credit limit? Some banks issue several cards on the same limit. If they share, Kashio will put the same statement date, due date, and amount on all of them.
cards.removeLead: Remove {card} from Credit cards? It stays hidden after Refresh. Your transactions are not deleted.
cards.datesLeadBoth: No statement-generation or due-date SMS was found for {card}. Enter each date. Do not reuse one for the other.
cards.datesLeadBothAmount: No statement SMS was found for {card}. Enter the statement date, payment due date, and total due. Do not reuse one date for the other.
cards.datesLeadStatement: No statement-generation SMS was found for {card}. Enter the statement date — not the payment due date.
cards.datesLeadDue: No due-date SMS was found for {card}. Enter the payment due date — not the statement date.
cards.datesLeadAmount: No statement SMS was found for {card}. Type the total due from the bank app or the statement PDF.
cards.datesStatementHint: The day the bank creates the bill each month. This is not the last day to pay.
cards.datesDueHint: The last day to pay this bill. This is not the statement date.

faq.intro: The short answer to “how do I do that?”, with the taps written out. Tap a question to open it, or search for a word like theme, budget or delete.
faq.qAddTxn: How do I add an expense or an income?
faq.aAddTxn:
The + button in the middle of the bottom bar opens Add Transaction from anywhere in the app. Choose Expenses or Income, tap the category it belongs to, then enter the amount and the date.

Paid with / Received in on the same screen decides which account the money leaves or lands in, so pick the right one if you keep more than one account. You have to be signed in to save.
faq.qCardTxn: How do I record a credit card spend or a card bill payment?
faq.aCardTxn:
The Credit card tab in Add Transaction appears once you have a credit card account. It offers two things: Credit card expense for something you bought on the card, and Credit card bill for the payment you make to the card company.

Keeping them apart matters. A card bill is treated as money moving from your bank to the card, not as a second expense, so paying the bill does not count the same spending twice.
faq.qEditTxn: How do I correct a transaction I already saved?
faq.aEditTxn:
Open the transaction list from the Explore row on the first screen — tapping the Expenses or Income total there takes you to the same list. Tap the transaction to open its details, then Edit, change what is wrong, and Update.

You can change the amount, category, date, note and account. The list only shows the month you have selected, so move to that month first if the transaction is older.
faq.qDeleteTxn: How do I delete one transaction?
faq.aDeleteTxn:
Tap the transaction in the list to open its details, then Delete. It asks you to confirm first, because a deleted transaction cannot be brought back.

Deleting a card bill payment removes both sides of it at once, so the bank and the card both go back to what they were.
faq.qDeleteMany: How do I delete several transactions at once?
faq.aDeleteMany:
All transactions is the only list with tick boxes. Tap each row you want, or use Select all for everything currently shown, then Delete and confirm. The bar at the bottom keeps count of what you have picked.

Set the year, month and day filters at the top first — that is the quickest way to clear one month, and it keeps Select all from picking up transactions you meant to keep.
faq.qTheme: How do I change the colours of the app?
faq.aTheme:
Themes lists every colour set, and tapping one applies it everywhere immediately — no restart, and nothing else changes.

A few themes are marked for Premium. If you do not subscribe, you can unlock one with diamonds from the Diamonds screen instead.
faq.qAvatar: How do I change my picture or pick a character?
faq.aAvatar:
Your picture lives on My Profile. Tap it, then choose Classic — your initial in the theme colour — or one of the 3D characters.

Characters are a Premium extra, and can also be unlocked with diamonds for a limited number of days. The Diamonds screen shows the cost and how long an unlock lasts.
faq.qAppLock: How do I lock the app with my fingerprint?
faq.aAppLock:
App lock uses the fingerprint, face or screen lock the phone already has, so there is no separate password to remember and nothing extra stored. Turning it on asks you to confirm once, to be sure it works.

After that the app asks when you open it, and again when you come back to it after a while — not every time you glance at a notification. If you later remove the screen lock from the phone, the app stops asking rather than shutting you out of your own records.
faq.qLanguage: How do I change the language?
faq.aLanguage:
Language lists every language the app is available in. Tap one and the whole app switches straight away, including this FAQ.

The legal wording in Terms of Use and Privacy Policy stays in English, since that is the version that legally applies. Everything else is translated.
faq.qImportSms: How do I turn my bank SMS into transactions?
faq.aImportSms:
Import transactions reads the bank messages already on this phone for the month you choose, and lists what it recognised as expenses, income and card bill payments. Tick the ones you want, correct any category, then Add transactions.

Raw SMS text stays on this phone. If you save an import and Premium cloud sync is on, those saved records can be stored in the cloud. Anything already imported is marked so you cannot add it twice. Reading SMS is Android only — Apple does not let any app do it.
faq.qAutoImport: Can bank SMS be added without me importing them every time?
faq.aAutoImport:
Yes. Switch on Add them automatically on the Import transactions screen and matched messages become transactions on their own each time you open the app.

It is off until you turn it on, it needs SMS access to be allowed already, and it only runs while the app is open. The same screen still lists everything, so you can check what it added and delete anything you did not want.
faq.qAddAccount: How do I add a bank account or a credit card?
faq.aAddAccount:
Accounts holds everywhere your money sits. Use + Add account, give it a name, enter what is in it today as the starting balance, and pick the type — Bank / Cash / Debit Card, or Credit Card.

The type is what keeps card spending out of your bank balance, so a credit card should be added as Credit Card and not as a bank account.
faq.qEditAccount: How do I rename or delete an account?
faq.aEditAccount:
Each account card on the Accounts screen has Edit for the name, starting balance and type, and Delete for the account itself.

One bank account and one credit card always have to remain, whatever you have named them, so the last of each cannot be deleted. Add the replacement first and the old one can then go.
faq.qCategory: How do I add or rename a category?
faq.aCategory:
Categories has a tab for Expenses and one for Income. Tap any category to rename it or change its icon and colour, or use + Add expense category at the bottom for a new one.

Renaming carries the old transactions and its budget across, so nothing is orphaned. Deleting a category moves whatever used it to Others, and Others itself cannot be deleted.
faq.qBudget: How do I set a monthly budget?
faq.aBudget:
The Budget tab is where limits live. Tap SET BUDGET, choose the category, enter the amount and save. Each budget then shows a bar of how much of it you have spent this month.

The ⋮ on a budget card lets you edit or remove it, and Copy from previous month brings last month's limits forward instead of typing them again.
faq.qReminder: How do I set a reminder?
faq.aReminder:
Open Reminders from the row above the tabs and pick the kind you need: bill or expense reminders, medicines, grocery expiry dates, or a general note. Each one has a New tab where you fill in the details and save.

Reminders arrive as phone notifications, so they reach you with the app closed. That needs notification permission, which the app asks for once, and phones that manage battery aggressively can still hold an alert back. Whether reminders make a sound or vibrate is up to you in Alarms & notifications.
faq.qBuyList: How do I use the buy list?
faq.aBuyList:
Buy list, in the row above the tabs, is for things you plan to purchase. Type the item and quantity, add it, and tick each one off at the shop.

It stays a list on its own: ticking an item does not create an expense, and it does not send anything to reminders.
faq.qSplit: How do I split an expense with friends?
faq.aSplit:
Split, in the row above the tabs, keeps shared spending. Add friends or a group first, then add the expense on the Expenses tab, choose who shares it, and save. Balances shows who owes whom after everything is counted up.

Split is a Premium feature, so it asks you to see the plans if your account does not have it.
faq.qCharts: Where do I see where my money went?
faq.aCharts:
The Charts tab breaks the selected month down by category as a ring, and can show income instead of expenses. Change the year, month or day at the top to look at another period.

The Budget tab answers the other half of it — what you planned to spend against what you actually spent.
faq.qBackup: How do I take a backup of my data?
faq.aBackup:
Backup data writes everything — transactions, accounts, budgets, reminders and the buy list — into one file you can send to yourself or keep in cloud storage.

Do this before changing phones or reinstalling the app. Backup is a Premium feature. Export Data is a different thing: a spreadsheet to read, not a file you can restore from.
faq.qRestore: How do I get my data back on a new phone?
faq.aRestore:
Install the app, sign in with the same account, then use Restore backup and pick the file you saved.

Restoring replaces what is in the app now, so it warns you before it goes ahead. If you had Premium with cloud sync on, your data comes back on sign-in without a file at all.
faq.qSignIn: Why do I need to sign in?
faq.aSignIn:
Signing in with Google is what lets the app save anything. Without it you can look around, but adding and editing are blocked, and nothing is kept.

It also ties your data to you rather than to the phone, so a lost phone does not have to mean lost records.
faq.aSignOut:
Log out sits at the bottom of the Profile screen and asks you to confirm.

Signing out does not delete anything. Sign in with the same account and your data is there again. To remove your data instead, use Delete all data in App settings.
faq.aPremium:
Premium Member on the Profile screen opens the comparison, which lists every feature and marks what is free and what needs a plan. In short: cloud sync, file backup and restore, split expenses, Smart Insights, all themes and the character avatars, and no ads.

Everything to do with tracking money day to day — transactions, accounts, budgets, charts, reminders, the buy list and SMS import — is free.
faq.aDiamonds:
Diamonds are earned by watching a short video, up to a few a day, and are spent on the Diamonds screen to unlock things without paying: a theme, a character avatar, or a pass that switches Premium features on for a set number of days.

A diamond pass does not remove ads — ads are what earn the diamonds. Inviting a friend also earns some.
faq.qHomeMonth: Why don't the app's monthly totals match my bank balance?
faq.aHomeMonth:
The first screen is a report on the month you are looking at: Expenses and Income are that month's totals, and Balance is one minus the other. It is not the money you have.

What you actually hold is on the Accounts screen, which counts every month together with each account's starting balance. The credit card row works the same way — what was spent on the card this month, and what was paid towards it.
faq.qContact: How do I report a problem or ask for a feature?
faq.aContact:
Feedback in App settings sends a message straight to us, and the first screen has Report an issue and Request a feature for the same thing.

Saying which screen you were on and what you expected instead makes a problem far quicker to find. Help and Terms of Use cover how each part of the app is meant to work.

terms.guide3Body:
The sections below walk through every feature in the order you are likely to meet it, from the Home screen through to your account and data. Each one describes what the feature does and how it behaves, so you know what you are agreeing to use.

Some features can be switched off, priced differently, or released gradually by the publisher, so what you see in the App is always the final word. Amounts and prices named here are defaults and may change.
terms.guide31Body:
The band at the top of Home shows Expenses, Income and Balance for the current calendar month. Tapping Expenses or Income opens the matching list.

When you have a credit card, a second row sits underneath with two figures for the month: what you charged to your cards, and what you paid towards their bills. A card bill you paid also counts as money out of the account that paid it, so the two rows together account for everything you spent.

You can hide the summary band, choose whether Home opens on Expenses or Income, and set how transactions are sorted, in App Settings under Home page.
terms.guide32Body:
The + button opens the add form. Choose Expense, Income or Credit card, pick a category, then enter the amount, the account it came from or went to, the date, and an optional note.

You can attach a photo of a bill to a transaction. Grocery entries can be broken into individual items with expiry dates, which can raise grocery reminders for you automatically.

Any transaction can be edited or deleted later by tapping it in a list.
terms.guide33Body:
A credit card is not a pot of money, so the App keeps it separate from the accounts that hold real money. What you charge to the card is an expense on the card, and “Credit card bill” records paying the card off as a transfer from the account that paid it to the card.

The bill counts as money out of the paying account, while the individual spends stay counted on the card, so the same money is never counted twice. Home and the Transactions summary show both figures for the month: charged to the card, and paid towards it.

The App does not track your credit limit or the headroom left on it. Only your bank knows the limit and which spends a statement covered, so any figure the App worked out from your messages alone could be wrong. Check your card statement for the limit available to you.
terms.guide34Body:
Accounts are where your money sits. There are two kinds: a money account, shown as Bank / Cash / Debit Card, and a Credit Card. You can add more accounts, rename them, give them an icon, or hide one you no longer use.

For a money account the App shows what existed up to the end of last month, this month's income and expenses, and the resulting balance. For a credit card it shows what was charged to it and what was paid towards it this month, and its balance reads as a negative figure for as long as it owes.

Balances are worked out from your starting balance plus everything you have recorded since. The App never contacts your bank to check them.
terms.guide35Body:
The Transactions screen lists your income or expenses for a chosen day, month or year. A row of chips lets you narrow the list to a single account, and the total for that filtered view is shown alongside.

The summary at the top mirrors Home: Expenses, Income and Balance for your money accounts, with what was charged to your credit cards and what was paid towards them on their own row underneath.

App Settings also offers an All transactions view, where you can filter by period, select many rows at once, and delete them together.
terms.guide36Body:
On Android the App can read bank messages already in your inbox and turn them into draft transactions. It asks for SMS permission first, and you can refuse. Messages are read on your device and are not uploaded anywhere.

It scans a recent window of messages, works out the amount, date, merchant, whether it was money in or out, and which account or card was used, then guesses a category from the merchant name. Messages that are not transactions, such as one-time passwords, failed payments, statements, due-date notices and loan or credit-limit offers, are filtered out.

Cash taken out of an ATM is skipped on purpose. Your bank balance and the cash in your hand sit in the same account, so the withdrawal moves nothing between them, and what you spend the cash on is the entry worth having. Drawing cash on a credit card is borrowing, so that is still imported.

Nothing is saved until you confirm. You can select or clear everything, untick individual rows, and change a category before importing. Rows you have already imported are remembered and will not be added twice.

Where SMS is unavailable you can paste message text instead. Imported entries are only as accurate as the messages they came from, and you are responsible for checking them.
terms.guide37Body: Transactions are grouped into categories such as Groceries, Food, Transport, Rent, EMI, bills and Salary. You can add your own with a chosen icon and colour, rename or delete the ones you added, and reset the list back to the defaults. The Others category cannot be removed, so nothing is ever left without a home.
terms.guide38Body: You can set a monthly limit for any expense category and watch what you have spent against it, including copying last month's limits into this one. Budgets are a guide for you; the App does not block spending or stop you recording a transaction that goes over one.
terms.guide39Body:
Charts show where your money went as a category breakdown, along with spending trends and a month-to-month comparison. The Calendar shows each day of a month with its totals, and tapping a day lists that day's entries.

Smart Insights reads your own recorded data on your device and points out things like a budget you are close to passing, a category that jumped compared with last month, or a month with no income recorded. Insights are observations about what you entered, not advice, and are a Premium feature.
terms.guide310Body: A cash book is a separate set of accounts, transactions and budgets, so you can keep, for example, home and business records apart. You start with one called Personal, and you can create more, rename them, change their icon, archive ones you have finished with, or delete them. Only the book you have open is shown anywhere in the App.
terms.guide311Body:
The Reminders workspace covers recurring bills, medicines with morning, afternoon and evening doses, groceries approaching their expiry date, and plain general reminders. You can set how far ahead you are warned, what time the daily alert arrives, and how long an alarm rings, and you can test an alarm at any time.

Reminders are a convenience only. Whether one actually reaches you depends on your device's settings, permissions, battery state and operating system limits, so please do not rely on them for anything critical.
terms.guide312Body:
The Shopping workspace keeps a simple list of items with quantities that you can search and tick off as bought.

The Split workspace lets you share costs with friends and groups, dividing an amount equally, by exact amounts, by percentage, by shares or with adjustments, and keeps a running record of who owes what. It needs a signed-in account and is a Premium feature. The App only keeps the record; it never moves money between you and anyone else.
terms.guide313Body: Search from the header looks across your transactions, reminders, shopping items and settings. You can change the display currency from the header chip, which changes how amounts are shown and does not convert them. The App is available in many languages. This guide is translated too, while the legal sections of the Terms of Use are given in English.
terms.guide314Body: You can change the look of the App with themes and give your profile a character avatar. A free theme is always available, and the rest can be unlocked with Premium or rented with diamonds.
terms.guide315Body:
Diamonds are an in-app reward with no cash value. They cannot be bought, sold, transferred or exchanged for money, and they are not refundable.

You earn them by choosing to watch a rewarded advertisement through to the end, and by inviting friends. There is a limit on how many you can earn from advertisements each day. Your balance and the daily limit are held and checked on our server using server time, so changing your device's clock will not increase what you can earn.

You can spend diamonds on a Premium pass lasting a set number of days, or on individual extras such as an avatar, a theme, or Smart Insights for a period. A pass or an unlock bought with diamonds gives you the feature for its stated time only, after which it simply ends. Prices, the reward per advertisement and the daily limit are shown in the App and can change at any time.

A Premium pass earned with diamonds unlocks features but does not remove advertisements. Only paid Premium is advertisement-free.
terms.guide316Body:
Each signed-in account gets its own invite code. If a friend enters your code, both of you receive diamonds, subject to a limit on how many invites are rewarded.

A code can only be used once per person, you cannot use your own, and we may withhold rewards where we believe codes are being abused, for example through duplicate or automated accounts.
terms.guide317Body:
Free use keeps your records on your device, shows advertisements, and leaves some features locked. Plus unlocks individual features you choose, and Premium unlocks everything, removes advertisements, and enables cloud sync.

Payment is made manually by UPI, after which you send us the payment reference and we activate your account. Activation is therefore not instant. Prices, plan contents and billing periods are shown in the App and may change; changes do not affect a period you have already paid for.
terms.guide318Body:
Free users may see banner and native advertisements in parts of the App, and may choose to watch rewarded video advertisements to earn diamonds. Watching a rewarded advertisement is always your choice and is never required to use a feature you already have.

Advertisements are supplied by third parties and are subject to their own terms and privacy policies. Paid Premium removes them.
terms.guide319Body:
With Premium and a signed-in account, your cash books, transactions, budgets, reminders, categories and attached bill images can sync so you can pick up on another device. Sync needs a working connection and can be delayed or incomplete, so please do not treat it as your only copy.

Cloud storage generally keeps around the last two years of dated records. Older entries stay on the device that created them.

You can only be signed in on one device at a time; signing in elsewhere ends the earlier session.
terms.guide320: 3.20 Backup, export and deleting your data
terms.guide320Body:
Premium lets you save a backup file of your data and restore it later. Restoring replaces what is currently on the device, and looking after the file is your responsibility. You can also export your transactions as a spreadsheet for a date range you choose.

You can delete your data at any time: from this device, from the cloud, or both. Deletion is permanent, so take a backup first if you may want the records again.
terms.guide321: 3.21 Using the App as a guest
terms.guide321Body: You can look around most of the App without an account. Saving your own records, importing messages, earning or spending diamonds, and syncing all need you to sign in, which you can do with Google, Apple or an email address and password.
terms.guide322Body:
App settings has a Delete account option. We ask why you are leaving, and once you confirm, the account is switched off straight away: you are signed out, you cannot sign in again, and everything held on that phone is erased. Take a backup first if you may want the records.

The request then goes to an administrator, who removes the account and its cloud copy from our records. Until that happens the account stays switched off and unusable. If you closed it by mistake, write to support quickly and it may be possible to put it back.

Expenses you shared in Split stay with the friends you shared them with, so their balances still add up. The reason you gave is kept without your name, as a statistic.

faq.qNotifications: What shows up under the bell?
faq.aNotifications: The bell next to the currency holds whatever is waiting on you: bills coming due or already late, groceries about to go off, medicines not taken yet, budgets you have gone past this month, friend requests and settlements to confirm in Split, and transactions the app added from your SMS. Rows leave on their own once you deal with the thing behind them, so an empty bell means nothing needs you.
faq.qDeleteAccount: How do I delete my account?
faq.aDeleteAccount: Open App settings and tap Delete account. Pick a reason, then confirm. Your account is switched off immediately, you are signed out, and everything on this phone is erased — so take a backup first if you might want the records. An admin then removes the account and its cloud copy from our records. Split expenses you shared stay with your friends so their balances still add up.
